arxiv-1805-00919.title: Flare Forecasting Using the Evolution of McIntosh Sunspot Classifications
arxiv-1805-00919.creator: A. E. McCloskey, P. T. Gallagher, D. S. Bloomfield
arxiv-1805-00919.description: Abstract Most solar flares originate in sunspot groups, where magnetic field changes lead to energy build-up and release. However, few flare-forecasting methods use information of sunspot-group evolution, instead focusing on static point-in-time observations. Here, a new forecast method is presented based upon the 24-hr evolution in McIntosh classification of sunspot groups. Evolution-dependent ⩾ \geqslant C1.0 and ⩾ \geqslant M1.

arxiv-2105-12448.title: The minimal Cremona degree of quartic surfaces
arxiv-2105-12448.creator: Massimiliano Mella
arxiv-2105-12448.description: Abstract . Two birational projective varieties in ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} are Cremona Equivalent if there is a birational modification of ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} mapping one onto the other. The minimal Cremona degree of X ⊂ ℙ n X\subset\mathbb{P}^{n} is the minimal integer among all degrees of varieties that are Cremona Equivalent to X X .

arxiv-2110-10105.title: Spatio-temporal modelling of phenotypic heterogeneity in tumour tissues and its impact on radiotherapy treatment.
arxiv-2110-10105.creator: Giulia L. Celora, Helen M. Byrne, P.G. Kevrekidis
arxiv-2110-10105.description: Abstract We present a mathematical model that describes how tumour heterogeneity evolves in a tissue slice that is oxygenated by a single blood vessel. Phenotype is identified with the stemness level of a cell, s s , that determines its proliferative capacity, apoptosis propensity and response to treatment.

arxiv-2201-08606.title: A test for fractal boundaries based on the basin entropy Journal: Commun. Nonlinear Sci. Numer. Simul.
arxiv-2201-08606.creator: Andreu Puy, Alvar Daza, Alexandre Wagemakers, Miguel A.F. Sanjuán
arxiv-2201-08606.description: Abstract In dynamical systems, basins of attraction connect a given set of initial conditions in phase space to their asymptotic states. The basin entropy and related tools quantify the unpredictability in the final state of a system when there is an initial perturbation or uncertainty in the initial state.

arxiv-2206-15117.title: A GPU-based Imager with Polarised Primary-beam Correction
arxiv-2206-15117.creator: Chris J. Skipper* \affref ref1, Anna M. M. Scaife \affref ref1 \affref ref2, J. Patrick Leahy \affref ref1
arxiv-2206-15117.description: Abstract The next generation of radio telescopes will strive for unprecedented dynamic range across wide fields of view, and direction-dependent gains such as the gain from the primary-beam pattern, or leakage of one Stokes product into another, must be removed from the cleaned images if dynamic range is to reach its full potential.

arxiv-2405-06215.title: Correlation functions and characteristic lengthscales in flat band superconductors
arxiv-2405-06215.creator: M. Thumin, G. Bouzerar
arxiv-2405-06215.description: Abstract Résumé The possibility of an unconventional form of high temperature superconductivity in flat band (FB) material does not cease to challenge our understanding of the physics in correlated systems. Here, we calculate the normal and anomalous one-particle correlation functions in various one and two dimensional FB systems and systematically extract the characteristic lengthscales.

arxiv-2504-17068.title: In-Context Learning can distort the relationship between sequence likelihoods and biological fitness
arxiv-2504-17068.creator: Pranav Kantroo 1,6, , Günter P. Wagner 2,3,4 , Benjamin B. Machta 5,6, 1 Computational Biology and Bioinformatics Program, Yale University, New Haven, CT-06520, USA 2 Emeritus, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Yale University, New Haven, CT-06520, USA 3 Department of Evolutionary Biol
arxiv-2504-17068.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pranav Kantroo 1,6, , Günter P. Wagner 2,3,4 , Benjamin B. Machta 5,6, 1 Computational Biology and Bioinformatics Program, Yale University, New Haven, CT-06520, USA 2 Emeritus, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Yale University, New Haven, CT-06520, USA 3 Department of Evolutionary Biol. Language models have emerged as powerful predictors of the viability of biological sequences. During training these models learn the rules of the grammar obeyed by sequences of amino acids or nucleotides.

arxiv-2505-24658.title: MATE: Diagnosing Empathy Calibration Failures in Multi-Turn Human–LLM Interaction
arxiv-2505-24658.creator: Yeseon Hong, Junhyuk Choi, Minju Kim, Bugeun Kim
arxiv-2505-24658.description: Abstract Large language models are increasingly used in emotionally consequential interactions. Response-level evaluation, however, struggles to diagnose how empathy fails across turns. We introduce MATE ( M ulti-turn A ssessment of calibra T ed E mpathy), a framework that evaluates empathy as a multi-turn, perception-centered process.

arxiv-2507-10668.title: Entanglement and Purity in Open Systems: A Breakdown of the Lindblad Approach
arxiv-2507-10668.creator: R. Serao, A. Quaranta, A. Capolupo, F. Franchini, S.M. Giampaolo
arxiv-2507-10668.description: Abstract We examine the effectiveness of Lindblad master equation in capturing the short-time dynamics of entanglement and purity in open quantum systems. Focusing on two interacting two-level systems interacting with a larger environment, we compare the Lindbladian approach to a full microscopic treatment.

arxiv-2507-11160.title: Efficient Canonical Correlation Analysis with Sparsity
arxiv-2507-11160.creator: Zixuan Wu
arxiv-2507-11160.description: Abstract In high-dimensional settings, Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) often fails, and existing sparse methods force an untenable choice between computational speed and statistical rigor. This work introduces a fast and provably consistent sparse CCA algorithm (ECCAR) that resolves this trade-off.

arxiv-2512-21697.title: GaDE - GPU-acceleration of time-dependent Dirac Equation for exascale Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-2512-21697.creator: Johanne Elise Vembe, Marcin Krotkiewski, Magnar Bjørgve, Morten Førre, Hicham Agueny *
arxiv-2512-21697.description: Abstract Modern heterogeneous high-performance computing (HPC) systems powered by advanced graphics processing unit (GPU) architectures enable accelerating computing with unprecedented performance and scalability. Here, we present a GPU-accelerated solver for the three-dimensional (3D) time-dependent Dirac Equation optimized for distributed HPC systems.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-charles-garni.title: Charles Garnier (Catholic Encyclopedia article)
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-charles-garni.creator: Lionel Lindsay
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-charles-garni.description: Article 'Charles Garnier' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

pmc-10735770.title: CASUAL EFFECTS OF EARLY-LIFE ADVERSITY AND MID/LATE-LIFE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTION ON THE PACE OF BIOLOGICAL AGING
pmc-10735770.creator: Daniel Belsky, Luigi Ferrucci
pmc-10735770.description: Epigenetic clocks have taken gerontology by storm. With the advent of 2nd and 3rd generation epigenetic clocks, including GrimAge and DunedinPACE, the field now has genomic biomarkers of aging that exhibit strong and consistent associations with aging-related morbidity and mortality. But the causes of variation in these powerful indices of aging-related biological changes remain poorly understood.

pmc-11467315.title: Biosynthesis of calcium oxide nanoparticles by employing Mulberry (Morus nigra) leaf extract as an efficient source for Rhodamine B remediation
pmc-11467315.creator: Gulnaz Nasir, Fozia Batool, Sobia Noreen, Humaira Yasmeen Gondal, Muhammad Mustaqeem, Zohaib Saeed, Yasmeen Gul, Fayyaz Ur Rehman, Hayssam M Ali
pmc-11467315.description: Green processes for synthesizing nanocomposites are a hot area of research today as traditional processes are expensive, inefficient, harmful for synthesizing organic and inorganic molecules, and unsuitable for large-scale operations. The present study investigates the capacity of green synthesized Calcium oxide nanoparticles (CaO NPs) for efficiently removing Rhodamine B.

pmc-11500171.title: sChemNET: a deep learning framework for predicting small molecules targeting microRNA function
pmc-11500171.creator: Diego Galeano, Imrat, Jeffrey Haltom, Chaylen Andolino, Aliza Yousey, Victoria Zaksas, Saswati Das, Stephen B. Baylin, Douglas C. Wallace, Frank J. Slack, Francisco J. Enguita, Eve Syrkin Wurtele, Dorothy Teegarden, Robert Meller, Daniel Cifuentes, Afshin Beheshti
pmc-11500171.description: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) have been implicated in human disorders, from cancers to infectious diseases. Targeting miRNAs or their target genes with small molecules offers opportunities to modulate dysregulated cellular processes linked to diseases. Yet, predicting small molecules associated with miRNAs remains challenging due to the small size of small molecule-miRNA datasets.

pmc-11677723.title: Pathological In Vivo Analysis of Helicobacter DNA Infection in Stomach Cells Using Carbon Nanotube Microsensor
pmc-11677723.creator: Kyung Lee, Sihyun Jun, Yeseul Oh, Seojun Lee, Ye Jun Oh, Keum Sook Kim, Suw Young Ly, Norma Velazquez Guadarrama, Piotr B Heczko, Ma Guadalupe Aguilera-Arreola
pmc-11677723.description: The WHO has classified Helicobacter pylori as a group 1 carcinogen for stomach cancer since early 1994. However, despite the high prevalence of Helicobacter pylori infection, only about 3% of infected people eventually develop gastric cancer.Biomolecular detections of Helicobacter pylori(HP) were compared using specially modified sensors and fluorine immobilized on a carbon nanotube (HFCNT) electrode, which yielded sensitive results.

pmc-11693000.title: MEETING THE CHALLENGE: NEURAL RESPONSE ASSOCIATED WITH MINIMAL DUAL-TASK COST IN AGING
pmc-11693000.creator: Claudia Schneider, Sophie Molholm, John Foxe, Johanna Wagner, Pierfilippo De Sanctis
pmc-11693000.description: Walking while engaged in a cognitively challenging task is a common daily activity that becomes harder as we grow older. The cost associated with performing two tasks simultaneously, called dual-task cost (DTC), can predict fall risk and cognitive decline. However, findings are mixed and predictive validity is modest.

pmc-11713407.title: Optimization of SHIP1 Inhibitors for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11713407.creator: Cynthia D Jesudason, Peter Bor‐Chian Lin, Disha Soni, Bridget M Perkins, Audrey Lee‐Gosselin, Cynthia M Ingraham, Will Hamilton, Emily R Mason, Omar El Jordi, Sarah Souza, Marlene Jacobson, Jerry Di Salvo, Brent Clayton, Shaoyou Chu, Jeffrey L Dage, Adrian L Oblak, Timothy I Richardson
pmc-11713407.description: BackgroundSHIP1 is a phosphatidyl inositol phosphatase encoded by INPP5D, which has been identified as a risk gene for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). SHIP1 is expressed in microglia, the resident macrophage in brain. It is a complex, multidomain protein that acts as a negative regulator downstream from TREM2.

pmc-12512441.title: Scurvy in the Modern Era: Revisiting a Forgotten Diagnosis in a Child With Chronic Recurrent Multifocal Osteomyelitis
pmc-12512441.creator: Rita Abou Zeid, Jessica Nicolas, Ghassan Dbaibo, Mira Merashli
pmc-12512441.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Scurvy, an ancient disease caused by severe vitamin C deficiency, continues to resurface in modern settings, especially among patients with selective eating habits due to developmental disorders, feeding difficulties, or low socioeconomic status. This report describes the case of a three-year-old child who presented with five weeks’ history of multisystemic symptoms, such as systemic (fever, generalized edema), musculoskeletal (bone pain), dermatological (petechiae), and mucosal (gingivitis), leading to a diagnostic dilemma.

pmc-13056735.title: Ribociclib is not a substrate or inhibitor of Oatp1b-mediated uptake in vivo
pmc-13056735.creator: Thomas Drabison, Eman A Ahmed, Nathan Colasanti, Robert H Weber, Alex Sparreboom, Eric D Eisenmann
pmc-13056735.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeRibociclib is a CDK4/6 inhibitor used to treat HR+/HER2- breast cancer. Despite regulatory documents suggesting that ribociclib may inhibit both CYP3A and OATP1B-type transport in vitro, it is unclear whether CDK4/6 inhibitors interact with these mechanisms in vivo.

pmc-13083294.title: Impact of group size and habitat disturbance on parasitic infection in free-ranging proboscis monkeys
pmc-13083294.creator: Muhammad Nur Fitri-Suhaimi, Liesbeth Frias, Elke Zimmermann, Primus Lambut, Joseph Tangah, Henry Bernard, Vijay Subbiah Kumar, Ikki Matsuda
pmc-13083294.description: Group-living primates experience the benefits and costs associated with sociality, including an elevated risk of parasite transmission. However, the relative influence of group type (i.e., social structure), group size, and habitat disturbance on parasitic infection remains unclear, particularly in Southeast Asian primates.

pmc-13241104.title: Severe dysgeusia and weight loss associated with terbinafine use: A case report
pmc-13241104.creator: Jacqueline J. Cavendish, Rebecca M. Garan, Mary M. Gibbs, Erika M. Harris
pmc-13241104.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Terbinafine is a widely used antifungal agent, with dysgeusia recognized as an uncommon and typically self-limited adverse effect. Severe or prolonged taste disturbance is exceedingly rare. We report the case of a 72-year-old woman who developed profound dysgeusia shortly after initiation of oral terbinafine for onychomycosis, manifesting as a persistent metallic taste, marked aversion to sweet foods, anorexia, and progressive unintentional weight loss.

pmc-13255952.title: Perioperative Risk of Palliative Gastrectomy in Advanced Gastric Cancer: A Nationwide Multicenter Analysis of Severe Complications and Mortality
pmc-13255952.creator: Sang-Ho Jeong, Miyeong Park, Kyung Won Seo, Inyoung Lee, Jeong Woo Kim, Jae-Seok Min, Sungsoo Park, Information Committee of the Korean Gastric Cancer Association
pmc-13255952.description: Simple SummaryPalliative surgery for advanced gastric cancer may help relieve symptoms such as bleeding or obstruction, but it can also cause serious harm after surgery. This study used a large nationwide dataset from the Korean Gastric Cancer Association to compare short-term outcomes between palliative surgery and curative gastrectomy in patients with gastric cancer.

pmc-13570615.title: Ex vivo Evaluation of Live-MB2 and CX-2 Biotic Strains on Inflammatory and Barrier-Related Biomarkers in a Human Skin Atopic Dermatitis–Like Model
pmc-13570615.creator: Sejin Cheon, Haeun Lee, Da Yeong Nam, Seokjun Kim, Kyeongeun Kim, Jaeyu Park, Dong-Geol Lee, Chun Ho Park, So Min Kang, Young Mok Heo, Hyun Ho Han, Dong Keon Yon
pmc-13570615.description: ObjectiveAtopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by epidermal barrier disruption and immune dysregulation. Live-MB2 and CX-2 were used in an ex vivo human skin AD-like model, which provides a biologically relevant platform for assessing cosmetic ingredients targeting AD-like features.
